At the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, McLaren’s Lando Norris converted his pole position into a commanding victory, securing his first Grand Prix win of the season. Though Norris lost the initial lead on the opening lap to teammate Oscar Piastri, a combination of superior mid-race pace, a costly traffic delay for Piastri with Carlos Sainz, and Piastri’s subsequent gearbox retirement allowed Norris to comfortably take the checkered flag. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen claimed second place after a lengthy stint on used soft tyres, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli completed the podium in third, executing a masterful recovery drive for Mercedes from seventh on the grid. Behind them, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc inherited fourth place after his teammate, Lewis Hamilton, was demoted to fifth following a five-second time penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

Lewis Hamilton was handed a three-place grid penalty by the FIA stewards after unnecessarily impeding McLaren’s Oscar Piastri during the final moments of Qualifying for the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix. The Scuderia Ferrari driver had originally secured a front-row start in P2, missing out on pole position to Lando Norris by a mere 0.012 seconds. However, while traveling at a significantly reduced speed on the racing line at Turn 1 following his own hot lap, Hamilton blocked a fast-approaching Piastri and forced the Australian to abort his final flying lap. Though Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur accepted blame for informing the driver too late over the team radio, the stewards issued the standard grid drop, relegating Hamilton to P5 and promoting Charles Leclerc, Kimi Antonelli, and Piastri up the order.

Lando Norris snatched a dramatic pole position for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, delivering a blazing 1m 17.207s lap in the dying moments of Q3 to break Mercedes’ season-long qualifying streak. The McLaren driver edged out Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by a mere 0.012 seconds, capitalizing on an upgraded car package while a deteriorating Hungaroring track surface triggered chaotic final runs. Hamilton’s teammate Charles Leclerc secured third, while championship leader Kimi Antonelli placed fourth amidst post-session investigations regarding yellow flags. The final shootout was heavily disrupted by fading grip, highlighted by a late spin from Red Bull’s Max Verstappen that left him in sixth, and a mechanical breakdown that left Mercedes’ George Russell stranded in seventh

Ferrari dominated Friday practice at the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix, signaling their strength at the high-downforce Hungaroring circuit. Charles Leclerc topped Free Practice 1 with a blistering 1:19.075, finishing nearly half a second ahead of Max Verstappen despite a late mechanical issue that stopped his car. In Free Practice 2, Lewis Hamilton secured a Ferrari 1-2 by clocking the day’s fastest time of 1:18.729, edging out Leclerc by 0.148 seconds and McLaren’s Lando Norris by nearly half a second. The second session was briefly red-flagged following a crash by Franco Colapinto, while Lance Stroll missed FP2 entirely due to a rear suspension failure on his heavily upgraded Aston Martin during the opening hour.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from pole position to claim his sixth victory of the season. In a dramatic race at Spa-Francorchamps, the Mercedes rookie executed a late pass on Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc (P2), while Red Bull’s Max Verstappen rounded out the podium in third. Behind them, Lewis Hamilton took fourth despite an opening-lap collision that forced George Russell into a DNF, finishing just ahead of Oscar Piastri in fifth. The remaining top 10 positions saw incredible recovery drives, featuring Isack Hadjar in sixth after starting 21st, Lando Norris fighting up to seventh, Gabriel Bortoleto in eighth for Audi, and rookies Arvid Lindblad (P9) and Franco Colapinto (P10) completing the point-scoring positions.
